source.title: In-Air Evoked Potential Audiometry of Grey Seals (Halichoerus grypus) from the North and Baltic Seas

method: auditory brainstem response (ABR), in air, with in-ear headphones and adapted ear inserts delivering 5-cycle (2-1-2) tone pips; thresholds by visual detection and by single-point F-test; an electrophysiological threshold, not a behavioural audiogram
conditions: six grey seals sedated (midazolam plus ketamine or tiletamine/zolazepam): two rehabilitation animals from the Seal Centre Friedrichskoog (Germany) and four born at the Hel Marine Station (Poland) and released after weaning, although the abstract calls them wild seals; thresholds in dB re 20 µPa peak-equivalent SPL (peSPL); ten frequencies tested, 1 to 20 kHz, so 20 kHz is the top of the stimulus set and nothing was tested above it; no temperature stated
quote: The mean auditory thresholds were ≤40 dB re 20 µPa peak equivalent sound pressure level (peSPL) between 4–20 kHz and showed similar patterns to in-air behavioural hearing tests of other phocid seals between 3 and 20 kHz.
note: Band over which the mean ABR threshold was at or below 40 dB peSPL. ABR thresholds usually sit above behavioural ones. The 20 kHz edge is the top frequency tested. Grey seal, Halichoerus grypus (O. Fabricius, 1791), accepted in the Mammal Diversity Database.

source.authors: Ruser A, Dähne M, Sundermeyer J, Lucke K, Houser DS, Finneran JJ, Driver J, Pawliczka I, Rosenberger T, Siebert U
source.title: In-Air Evoked Potential Audiometry of Grey Seals (Halichoerus grypus) from the North and Baltic Seas

value: steep reduction in sensitivity below 3 kHz (lowest frequency tested 1 kHz)
method: auditory brainstem response (ABR), in air, with in-ear headphones and adapted ear inserts delivering 5-cycle (2-1-2) tone pips; thresholds by visual detection and by single-point F-test; an electrophysiological threshold, not a behavioural audiogram
conditions: six grey seals sedated (midazolam plus ketamine or tiletamine/zolazepam): two rehabilitation animals from the Seal Centre Friedrichskoog (Germany) and four born at the Hel Marine Station (Poland) and released after weaning, although the abstract calls them wild seals; thresholds in dB re 20 µPa peak-equivalent SPL (peSPL); ten frequencies tested, 1 to 20 kHz, so 20 kHz is the top of the stimulus set and nothing was tested above it; no temperature stated
quote: Below 3 kHz, a steep reduction in hearing sensitivity was observed, which differed from the rate of decline in sensitivity obtained in behavioural studies on other phocids.
note: The authors suggest the ear inserts or the structure of the distal ear canal may account for the steeper low-frequency decline, so the low-frequency roll-off may be partly a method effect. Nothing was tested below 1 kHz.

method: behavioural psychophysics in air: go/no-go pointing response to tones; 50% hit-rate threshold by signal detection methods; birds trained, not anaesthetised
conditions: four captive Humboldt penguins (two males, two females) tested in a foam-lined anechoic box in a training room; nine frequencies tested, 125 Hz to 10 kHz, so 10 kHz is the top of the stimulus set; thresholds in dB rms re 20 µPa; mean most sensitive threshold at 2 kHz 15 dB (SD 10.6, n = 4) in the Results; large inter-individual variation; temperature and ambient noise level not stated
quote: The 50% hit rate was found to be below 76 dB rms re 20 µPa between 0.250 kHz and 10 kHz, with most sensitive hearing at 2 kHz (mean threshold of 15.3 dB rms re 20 µPa).
note: Best frequency 2000 Hz. The range is the span of frequencies with a threshold below 76 dB, and its upper edge is the top frequency tested. The authors also report an unexpectedly low threshold at 0.250 kHz (mean 36.8 dB) after a rapid decline at 0.500 kHz (mean 64.1 dB) and cannot say whether this is an artefact of the methods. source.title: Spectral sensitivity and temporal resolution of the sexually dimorphic compound eyes of Electrogena lateralis

eye: female eye and male ventral eye region (green peak)
method: electroretinography (ERG) on excised-eye preparations, recording electrode in the eye, reference in the abdomen; flash method; the peaks are peaks of the whole-eye ERG spectral sensitivity, not measured pigment lambda max
conditions: adults; dark-adapted at least 40 min; number of preparations per group is in the paper's Table 1, which was not read; temperature not stated; pooled across female eye and male ventral region
quote: The male ventral eye region and female eye were most sensitive to the green spectral range, with major and minor peak sensitivities at 536 and 366 nm, respectively.
note: Major (green) ERG peak. Mayfly Electrogena lateralis (Curtis, 1834), accepted on GBIF. Male dorsal eye region differs (UV only).

source.title: Spectral sensitivity and temporal resolution of the sexually dimorphic compound eyes of Electrogena lateralis

method: electroretinography (ERG) on excised-eye preparations, recording electrode in the eye, reference in the abdomen; flash method; the peaks are peaks of the whole-eye ERG spectral sensitivity, not measured pigment lambda max
conditions: adult males; dark-adapted only (no chromatic adaptation for this region); number of preparations in Table 1, not read; temperature not stated
quote: The dorsal eye region of males was exclusively ultraviolet sensitive, with maximal sensitivity at 353 nm.
note: Males have a split eye; the dorsal region showed no green peak in this ERG.

source.authors: Egri Á, Jásdi M, Kriska G
source.title: Spectral sensitivity and temporal resolution of the sexually dimorphic compound eyes of Electrogena lateralis

method: electroretinographic flicker fusion frequency with stroboscopic stimuli, excised-eye preparations; UV stimulation only
conditions: adult males, 9 dorsal eye preparations tested (Methods: 6 female, 9 male ventral and 9 male dorsal); dark-adapted 40 min; value is mean with SD 32.7 Hz; light level and temperature not stated
quote: Mean ± SD of the FFF values obtained for the dorsal eyes was 148.7 Hz ± 32.7 Hz.
note: The authors report the dorsal value significantly higher than the ventral region of male eyes. Female (104.5 Hz) and male ventral (104.1 Hz) values are in the paper but their sentences could not be quoted whole, so they are not filed.

source.title: Spectral sensitivity and color discrimination of Euxesta eluta and Chaetopsis massyla (Diptera: Ulidiidae)

method: electroretinogram, flash method (200 ms pulses, 2 mV criterion response); peak of the ERG spectral sensitivity curve, not a pigment lambda max
conditions: ten individuals of each sex and species; dark-adapted 1 hr; recordings at 27 to 28 °C, 60 to 72 % relative humidity; abstract states the peak for both species together
quote: Using electroretinograms, spectral sensitivity curves for both species revealed broad curves with a peak in the UV (350 nm) and the green region (500–550 nm) of the spectrum.
note: Sexes similar in curve shape. The Results give about 350 nm and a broad green peak at 520 to 550 nm for both species. Quote covers E. eluta and Chaetopsis massyla together; only E. eluta is filed because the name Chaetopsis massyla could not be confirmed on an authority page.

source.title: Spectral sensitivity and color discrimination of Euxesta eluta and Chaetopsis massyla (Diptera: Ulidiidae)

method: electroretinogram, flash method (200 ms pulses, 2 mV criterion response); peak of the ERG spectral sensitivity curve, not a pigment lambda max
conditions: ten individuals of each sex and species; dark-adapted 1 hr; recordings at 27 to 28 °C, 60 to 72 % relative humidity; abstract states the peak for both species together
quote: Using electroretinograms, spectral sensitivity curves for both species revealed broad curves with a peak in the UV (350 nm) and the green region (500–550 nm) of the spectrum.
note: Green peak as given in the abstract (500 to 550 nm); the Results give a broad peak at about 520 to 550 nm. Quote covers E. eluta and Chaetopsis massyla together; only E. eluta is filed.

source.title: Spectral sensitivity and color discrimination of Euxesta eluta and Chaetopsis massyla (Diptera: Ulidiidae)

value: attracted to yellow cards only at low or high brightness and to mid-level bright blue cards; not attracted to green cards at any brightness
method: laboratory paired-choice assays: coloured cards paired with gray cards of matching brightness
conditions: laboratory cages of 35 to 40 flies, about equal sexes, four cages on four days; sexes pooled
quote: Euxesta eluta was only attracted to yellow cards at low or high brightness levels, to mid-level bright blue cards and not attracted to green cards at any brightness level.
note: Colour-card attraction in the laboratory; the other species in the paper responded differently (attracted to yellow and green, avoided blue).
